# A lattice-complete critical profile below individual Grünbaum efficiency

This is an exact counterexample to a proposed auxiliary statement, NOT to
(OC). It has an actual global deepest point, an actual regular critical
circuit, and a complete integer base. The maximum efficiency over the
entire normal-dependent nonnegative convex-potential cone is less than
Gamma_d. Its equal fiber volumes fail the strict no-heavy condition of
the attained-counterexample framework. That extra condition, and the
stronger proper-minor quotas, therefore remain material hypotheses.

## 1. The body and its complete integer base

Fix d>=2 and n=d. In the integer space R^d put

    v_0=(-1,...,-1),  v_i=e_i (1<=i<=d),
    B=conv(v_0,...,v_d),  P={0,v_0,...,v_d}.

Then B intersect Z^d=P. Indeed write an integer z in B as
z_i=t_i-t_0, with t_j>=0 and sum t_j=1. Every z_i>=-1. If one
coordinate equals -1, then t_0>=1, so t_0=1 and z=v_0. Otherwise all
coordinates are nonnegative integers and
sum z_i=1-(d+1)t_0<=1. Thus z is 0 or a unit vector. Every listed point
does belong to B. The vertices are affinely independent, and 0 is their
average and lies in the interior.

Let K be any d-simplex, with volume V>0, barycentric functions
lambda_0,...,lambda_d, and centroid g. The full-dimensional convex body

    C=B times K

has S=P times K and total mixed d-volume M=(d+2)V. Write
alpha=d/(d+1), Gamma=alpha^d.

## 2. Actual critical caps and exact global depth

Define linear base functions

    ell_0(z)=-sum_i z_i,
    ell_i(z)=(d+1)z_i-sum_l z_l  (1<=i<=d).

They sum to zero; ell_j(v_j)=d, ell_j(v_k)=-1 for k!=j, and ell_j(0)=0.
Use the d+1 ambient halfspaces

    H_j={lambda_j(x)-1/(d+1)+ell_j(z)>=0}.                 (1)

At 0 their traces are the centroid vertex caps of K, each of volume
Gamma V. At v_j the entire fiber is strictly contained, since its
minimum margin is d-1/(d+1)>0. At the other outer bases the entire
fiber is strictly missed, since its maximum margin is -1/(d+1)<0.
Consequently every cap has raw mass

    Q=(1+Gamma)V.                                       (2)

The margins in (1) sum identically to zero, so the closed caps cover the
whole ambient space. Every point of S is therefore contained in a cap
of mass Q, proving that the global maximum raw depth is at most Q.

For the reverse inequality take Y=(0,g). Any containing halfspace can
be moved parallel until its boundary passes through Y; this only
decreases captured mass. Write the resulting margin as

    a.z+u.(x-g).

Its trace on the own fiber captures at least Gamma V by the ordinary
simplex centroid Grünbaum inequality if u!=0. If u=0 it captures the
whole own fiber, which also gives this lower bound.

To count the outer fibers exactly, let X be uniform on K. For
j=0,...,d let X_j be the point obtained by cyclically permuting its
d+1 barycentric coordinates by j positions. Each X_j is uniform on K:
the corresponding affine vertex permutation preserves uniform volume.
Pointwise,

    sum_j X_j=(d+1)g,  sum_j v_j=0.

Hence the d+1 real numbers a.v_j+u.(X_j-g) sum to zero. At least one
is nonnegative, including when some or all are zero. Integrating the
sum of their closed-halfspace indicators and using the uniform
marginals proves

    sum_j |K intersect {x:a.v_j+u.(x-g)>=0}| >= V.         (3)

Together the own-fiber bound and (3) give depth at least Q at Y. Thus

    max_(y in S) depth_S(y)=(1+Gamma)/(d+2)=:beta.        (4)

This lower bound treats every ambient normal, including pure-integer
normals and every oblique normal, and counts boundary mass correctly.
No assertion about approximate centers or averaged candidate points is
used; the selected point is the single point Y.

Only the own fiber has a nonempty section of any cap boundary. That
section has centroid g: its j-th barycentric coordinate is 1/(d+1),
and the other d centroid coordinates are alpha/d=1/(d+1). Thus its
full mixed section centroid is Y. The continuous normals are
grad lambda_j and sum to zero. The coarea section masses, for these
unnormalized normals, all equal d alpha^(d-1)V. This follows either
by direct simplex scaling or by differentiating
|{lambda_j>=t}|=(1-t)^d V. The response weights of this positive
regular critical circuit are consequently theta_j=1/(d+1).
All other fibers are strictly separated from the cap boundaries.
The own proper sections meet the own boundary in surface-null sets.
There are no supporting-facet allocations or hidden derivative terms.

## 3. The entire convex-potential cone has exact optimum beta

Let eta be the sum of H_(d-1) on the boundaries of all fibers, marked
by the outward unit continuous normal u. Normals at facet intersections
can be chosen arbitrarily; those intersections are eta-null. Set

    W=(1/(d+1)) sum_j 1_(H_j).

On every outer fiber W=1/(d+1) identically. On the own fiber W is
the canonical simplex profile

    W_0(x)=(1/(d+1)) sum_j 1_{lambda_j(x)>=1/(d+1)}.

Consider any finite nonnegative potential Phi(u,z,x) that is convex in
(z,x) for each fixed u, is measurable on the normal bundle, and has
finite positive denominator. Define

    A=integral_(boundary K) Phi(u(x),0,x) dH_(d-1),
    I_j=integral_(boundary K) Phi(u(x),v_j,x) dH_(d-1),
    T=sum_(j=0)^d I_j.

Here A denotes the central-base integral, while I_j denotes the integral
at the explicitly indexed outer base v_j. Thus the denominator is A+T.

Since 0=(sum_j v_j)/(d+1), convexity at every fixed (u,x) gives

    A<=T/(d+1).                                      (5)

The independently proved simplex-facet convex-order inequality gives

    integral_(boundary K) Phi(u(x),0,x) W_0(x)
      dH_(d-1)(x) <= Gamma A.                        (6)

Precisely, on each facet the normal is constant and the restriction of
Phi is convex. The facet inequality in
`candidate 8e69e6820cd6ee00`
applies facet by facet, with no change to the Euclidean surface measure.
It is valid for every such finite convex restriction. A finite convex
function on the ambient space is continuous, so no boundary regularity
of the test is being assumed silently.

Equations (5)-(6) yield

    integral Phi W d eta / integral Phi d eta
       <= [Gamma A+T/(d+1)]/[A+T]
       <= (Gamma+1)/(d+2)=beta.                     (7)

For the second inequality, put r=A/T. A positive denominator and (5)
force T>0 and 0<=r<=1/(d+1). The ratio
(Gamma r+1/(d+1))/(r+1) increases in r, since
Gamma>1/(d+1). The latter strict inequality follows from Bernoulli:
alpha^(d-1)>=(2/(d+1)), so
Gamma>=2d/(d+1)^2>1/(d+1) for d>=2.

The constant test Phi=1 attains (7). All fibers have the same surface
measure, and the canonical simplex profile has facetwise average
Gamma, by the same facet identity with a constant test. Therefore

    sup_Phi integral Phi W d eta / integral Phi d eta
      =beta=(1+Gamma)/(d+2)<Gamma.                   (8)

This is an attained bound on the entire normal-dependent cone, not an
optimization over a chosen finite set of hinges or a numerical search.

## 4. Scope and the surviving quota-aware possibility

For d=2, Gamma=4/9, beta=13/36. With the standard continuous triangle
V=1/2, the raw depth is Q=13/18 and total mass is 2.

The d+2 bases have distinct parities when d>=2: 0, each unit vector,
and the all-ones parity of v_0. Thus k(P)=d+2 and every fiber has volume

    V=M/k(P).

In particular the strict no-heavy inequality V<M/k(P) fails by equality.
The example does not satisfy the quota hypotheses of an all-positive
attained bad minimum, and its depth is much larger than the OC target
Gamma/2^d. It disproves the universal individual-Gamma premise based
only on actual criticality, convex compatibility, and complete lattice
sampling. It does not disprove a premise retaining the strict proper-
minor quotas, nor a simultaneous test using fewer witnesses, nor (OC).

Independent audit PASS in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
the contributor reran the independent verifier: 1,350 exact checks PASS. The audit
also proves uniqueness of Y: outer bases have depth at most V/2<Q by
exposing isolation; at a different middle point x, a coordinate
lambda_j(x)>1/(d+1) gives a shifted cap with the same single full outer
fiber and a strictly smaller own cap. No global OC conclusion is inferred.
